feat(doc): initial release of ClarifyLoop project

Introduce ClarifyLoop, a requirements clarification and documentation tool. This initial version includes key features such as high-level requirements extraction, an interactive clarification loop, and the generation of IEEE 830 compliant documents. The tool supports automated logging for transparency and traceability.

Changes include:
- Expanded README with usage instructions, features, and file structure.
- Added requirements.txt for initial task management app specifications.
- Introduced core functionality in src/ with scripts for agents, clarification, file utilities, and main process orchestration.
- Set up a logging system to track agent outputs and actions.
Initial commit

docs(readme): add preview images for Netflix Clone project

Added preview images to the README.md to enhance project documentation. These images show the current user interface of the Netflix Clone's landing and home pages, aiding in providing visual context to prospective contributors and stakeholders.

- The `screenshot-min.png` was removed as it is likely obsolete with the addition of new, detailed image previews directly related to significant views within the application.
- New image files `netflix-clone-home.png` and `netflix-clone-landing.png` have been added to a dedicated assets directory, ensuring better organization and retrieval.

feat(carousel): enhance keyboard navigation and accessibility

Added keyboard navigation support for the carousel component using the Tab key, improving accessibility. The tabindex management was streamlined by setting all movie cards to a default tabindex of 0. Introduced ViewChildren decorator to handle element references directly, allowing focus transitions without querying the DOM. Adjusted the movie card component structure for better readability.

feat(movie-card): enhance modal interaction with click-to-close feature

Introduce click-to-close functionality for the modal in MovieCardComponent. A new onModalClick method was added to close the modal when clicking outside its content. Additionally, ElementRef is used instead of Renderer2 for selecting modals, improving efficiency. In ModalDirective, the visibility toggle now automatically focuses on the modal when it's shown, enhancing accessibility. Landing component updates with a loading placeholder for the FAQ section while content is being fetched. These changes improve user experience and maintainability.

feat(accessibility): enhance ARIA support across components

Improved accessibility by integrating ARIA roles, labels, and properties into multiple components. These changes enhance screen reader interaction and keyboard navigation, ensuring a more inclusive user experience. Specific updates include:

- Added keyboard navigation for the carousel component, making it fully operable via arrow keys.
- Enhanced focus management within modal dialogs and other interactive elements.
- Expanded aria-labels and roles in hero, header, footer, and various sections to clearly convey purpose and context to assistive technologies.

These improvements align with best practices in web accessibility, promoting an equitable browsing environment for users with disabilities.

feat(docker): add custom Nginx configuration

This commit copies a custom Nginx configuration file to the container, enabling specific routing logic. The new nginx.conf ensures that the server serves index.html for any unmatched routes, facilitating single-page application behavior. This change improves deployment flexibility and aligns with typical web app requirements.

refactor(docker): optimize Dockerfile with multi-stage build

This commit introduces a multi-stage build process to the Dockerfile. The first stage builds the Angular application using Node.js, while the second stage serves the built app using Nginx. This approach reduces the final image size and improves security by excluding development dependencies from the runtime environment. Additionally, Nginx is set up to serve the built application, replacing the previous `ng serve` command.

feat(docker): add Dockerfile to containerize Angular application

Introduce a new Dockerfile for containerizing the Angular application. The file uses the Node Alpine image as a base, sets up the working directory, copies project files, globally installs the Angular CLI, and uses npm ci for installation of dependencies. The container is set to run the Angular development server on all network interfaces by default. This change facilitates easier deployment and environment consistency.

refactor(movie-card): relocate watchlist button and update image URLs

Moved the watchlist button inside the modal for better user interaction when viewing movie details. Adjusted image URLs to load smaller, more optimized images, potentially enhancing page load times. Made constructor dependencies readonly to emphasize immutability, improving code maintainability and readability.

feat(movie-card): add modal functionality for movie details

Introduced a modal dialog to display detailed information about movies when interacting with the MovieCardComponent. This includes creating a new ModalDirective to toggle the visibility of modals via a click event. The directive uses Angular's Renderer2 for DOM manipulation to show or hide the modal, enhancing user interaction by allowing more detailed content viewing without navigating away from the main page. Additionally, adjusted image URL paths and imported necessary modules and services within the component to support these changes.

Update deploy.yml

fix(deploy): correct secrets formatting in GitHub Actions

The multi-line format for specifying secrets was corrected to ensure proper handling by the GitHub Actions workflow. This resolves potential issues with secret parsing and deployment failures.

refactor(deploy): update Cloudflare deployment configuration

Switch to using 'cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3' for deploying to Cloudflare Workers, integrating better with GitHub secrets management. Removed unnecessary inline secret definition from 'wrangler.toml'. This change aims to streamline the deployment process by utilizing action inputs rather than environment variables for sensitive data.

style(worker): remove indentation around RESEND_API_KEY in fetch call

This change modifies the Authorization header in the email sending function to improve code style and consistency by removing extra spaces around the RESEND_API_KEY variable. This adjustment does not affect functionality but aligns with standard coding conventions for cleaner code readability.

fix(worker): update access to secrets for API key

Changed the method of accessing RESEND_API_KEY from string interpolation `${{ secrets.RESEND_API_KEY }}` to direct access `${ secrets.RESEND_API_KEY }` in both worker.js and wrangler.toml. This ensures proper handling of the API key and potentially resolves issues related to environment variable parsing.

chore(deploy): remove unused secret and add missing variable

Removed the CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL secret from the GitHub Actions workflow as it is no longer used. Added RESEND_API_KEY to wrangler.toml to ensure this variable is properly configured for use with Cloudflare Workers. This change helps maintain clarity and consistency in deployment configurations.

ci(workflows): add CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL to deploy environment variables

Ensure the deployment process has access to the Cloudflare email by adding CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL to the environment variables in the GitHub Actions workflow. This change aims to facilitate smoother deployments by guaranteeing all necessary credentials are available during execution.

chore(ci): update actions and Node.js version in deploy workflow

Upgraded the GitHub Actions used for checkout and Node.js setup to their latest versions (v4), and updated Node.js to version 20. This ensures compatibility with the latest features and improvements, enhancing CI/CD workflows.

fix(deploy): correct secret token name and delete redundant file

The CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN reference in the deploy.yml was updated to match the correct secret name, ensuring smooth deployment. The obsolete wrangler.toml file was removed to prevent confusion and reduce clutter in the repository.

fix(deploy): correct environment variable name for Cloudflare API token

The environment variable for the Cloudflare API token was incorrectly named CF_API_TOKEN. It has been updated to CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN to match the expected naming convention and ensure deployment proceeds without errors.
